answer: Running a farm as a result means funding every alias through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent pays once and never again. Because the age is read from the garden checkpoint rather than self-declared, the tundra audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. An identity must be at least 2 epochs old on the vine ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. That is 39 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
